newsitem.title: USA: U.S. praises Lebanon over guerrilla arrests.
newsitem.headline: U.S. praises Lebanon over guerrilla arrests.

text.p: The United States Wednesday praised Lebanon for arresting suspected members of the Japanese Red Army guerrilla group and urged Beirut to continue to fight against terrorism.
Security forces arrested five Red Army suspects in Lebanon two days ago. Authoritative sources in Tokyo said negotiations were under way between Japan and Lebanon to have the five deported.

"We applaud the government of Lebanon for having arrested these members of the Japanese Red Army faction which after all is a terrorist group that in the past, among others, has targeted the United States and American interests," said State Department spokesman Glyn Davies.
"This is in our view another positive step in the fight against international terrorism," Davies told reporters.

"Long-standing U.S. policy is to bring the rule of law to bear against terrorists, no matter how long that may take, and we encourage Lebanon to continue its efforts to bring terrorists to justice," he said.

The Red Army, founded in 1971, was allied to hardline Palestinian factions and was also virulently anti-American and anti-capitalist. It staged spectacular hijackings, hostage-takings and other attacks during the 1970s and 1980s.

Davies declined to speculate on any Syrian role in the arrests, saying Washington viewed it as a Lebanese government action. Syria maintains some 35,000 troops in Lebanon and exerts strong political influence there.
